Index of the documentation for TabChat for Agents.

Updated 2026-10-15 · Source README.md

TabChat for Agents documentation

TabChat for Agents (the app is still called Tabchat) is a native macOS app that brings WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, Brightspace, Reddit, X, GitHub and any website into one window via a sidebar of service icons, all sharing the system's own web engine (WKWebView). Rewritten from scratch in Swift, macOS 14+, Apple Silicon only, targeting users who want a single native app instead of bouncing between browsers and standalone clients.

It also lets local AI agents read those services and act in them (open a chat, read contact details, download documents — never send) through a Unix socket, a CLI and MCP: see 04 Agent API. TabChat for Agents is an independent community port of MMV2408/tabchat; it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the original project.

Status: v0.1.1 released (2026-10-13); the agent API is built and live-tested on WhatsApp (2026-10-15). What's left is in the root README.md ("Still to do") and TASKS.md.

Terms used throughout

Term Meaning
WKWebView The system WebKit browser engine (same as Safari); used by Tabchat to display services
Service A web app or website (WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, etc.) shown in a sidebar tab
Tab One instance of a service; the app can have multiple tabs of the same service (e.g. two WhatsApp accounts)
Profile A WKWebsiteDataStore for one sign-in; shared by related services (e.g. Teams, Outlook, OneDrive via "microsoft-work")
Unread A count badge on a service tab, the Dock icon and menu bar
Focus macOS notification Focus modes; Tabchat respects them before showing notifications

What Tabchat is, the ideas behind it, and what is in and out of scope.

Updated 2026-10-15 · Source 01-overview.md · Read first: TabChat for Agents documentation

Overview

What it is

Tabchat is a native macOS app that brings messaging and productivity services—WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, Brightspace, and any website—into one window. Services appear as icons in a sidebar; each can have multiple accounts (e.g., two WhatsApp numbers) with separate sign-ins, except Teams/Outlook/OneDrive which share one Microsoft login.

The app reuses the system's WebKit engine (WKWebView), so it stays lightweight and integrates deeply with macOS: unread badges on the Dock icon and menu bar, native notifications that respect Focus modes, menu bar icon for always-at-hand access, start-at-login support.

Credit: Tabchat is a rewrite from scratch of MMV2408/tabchat, an Electron app for Linux (MIT License, © Mike Vijverberg). This fork is macOS-only; the original Linux code lives on the Linux branch (tag upstream-final).

TabChat for Agents. Since October 2026 the project's focus is letting the AI agents on the owner's Mac read these services and act in them — see 04 Agent API. It is an independent community port of MMV2408/tabchat, not affiliated with or endorsed by the original project.

The ideas behind it

  1. One app, not context-switching: Bring all your messaging and work apps into one place instead of Alt-Tab between browsers and standalone apps.
  2. Native and lightweight: Built in Swift with macOS system frameworks (SwiftUI, AppKit, WKWebView), not a bundled browser. The app itself is a few megabytes; all the heavy lifting is the web service.
  3. Unified notifications: Notifications arrive in one place, respect your Focus modes, and clicking one opens the right service in the window instead of a new window or tab.
  4. Deep macOS integration: The app lives in the menu bar when closed, updates Dock and menu bar badges, supports start-at-login via SMAppService, uses system theme (light/dark).
  5. Agents read what you can see: Agents get the services through the official web clients you are signed in to, read-only by default, never sending — the lowest-risk route to chats that have no personal-account API.

What's built (v0.1.1)

  • Sidebar of service icons with unread badges; drag to reorder; right-click menu
  • Services: WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook (work and personal), OneDrive, Brightspace, Reddit, X, GitHub, custom sites
  • Multiple accounts per service, each with its own sign-in; Teams, Outlook (work), OneDrive and Brightspace share one Microsoft sign-in by default
  • One WKWebsiteDataStore per sign-in; sign-ins survive restart
  • Unread counts on each tab, the Dock and the menu bar
  • Native notifications that respect Focus; clicking one opens its service; pause (1 hour, until tomorrow 08:00, until off) and per-tab mute
  • Closing the window keeps everything running; menu bar item; optional start at login, hidden
  • Find on page, downloads, back/forward/reload/home, offline screen with retry
  • Split view, Cmd+K quick switcher, tab sleep, duplicate and incognito tabs
  • Hide and reorder catalog cards; choose which browser opens links
  • Light/dark mode following the system

Not built, or not planned

  • Not yet: notarised build (Developer ID), Sparkle updates, Intel builds, unread counts for Reddit and GitHub (no count in their titles)
  • Not planned: iMessage (no web version; macOS can't embed another app's window); Linux (use the original)

What stays hard

  1. WebRTC in WKWebView on macOS: Teams and Discord calls, and Teams screen share. The engine spike confirmed these work, but edge cases (mute, camera, screen content) may need workarounds.
  2. School SSO for Brightspace: Some institutions use OIDC or SAML flows that might not survive WKWebsiteDataStore boundaries.
  3. Unread detection: Tabchat reads counts from page titles ((3) …, or • for "something unread"). Services that only show unread in a favicon or the page itself (Reddit, GitHub) would need per-service scripts, which are not built.

System components, data flow, and design decisions.

Updated 2026-10-15 · Source 02-architecture.md · Read first: TabChat for Agents documentation, Overview

Architecture

A SwiftUI app with AppKit where SwiftUI falls short (the main window's close behaviour, the web view container). Every tab is one WKWebView; every sign-in is one persistent WKWebsiteDataStore. Decision logic lives in plain types under App/Model/ so it can be unit tested without a window.

Source layout

App/
├── TabchatApp.swift         app entry: main Window, Settings scene, MenuBarExtra, AppDelegate
│                            (notification permission and clicks, Dock reopen)
├── Model/                   plain, testable types
│   ├── AppModel(+Features)  the observable model: tabs, selection, unread, split, sleep, Cmd+K
│   ├── AppState, AppSettings, Tab, Profile, Service   what is saved, and the service catalog
│   ├── StateStore           state.json in ~/Library/Application Support/Tabchat (atomic writes,
│   │                        schema v3, migrates v1 and v2)
│   ├── StableUUID           profile name → stable UUID → WKWebsiteDataStore(forIdentifier:)
│   ├── UnreadParser         "(3) …" → 3, "• …" → unread dot
│   ├── NotificationPause    1 hour / until tomorrow 08:00 / until off; stored as an end date
│   ├── SleepClock           which idle tabs to put to sleep
│   ├── SplitState           the two panes, focused side, divider ratio (20–80%)
│   ├── QuickSwitcher        Cmd+K ranking and actions
│   ├── LinkPolicy, LinkTarget, Browsers   where a link opens (in-app, default or chosen browser)
│   ├── CatalogLayout        hidden and reordered cards in the Add service sheet
│   ├── LoginItem            SMAppService.mainApp
│   └── DownloadNaming, IconCandidate, URLInput
├── Agent/                   the agent API (see 04 Agent API): socket server, service, feed,
│                            responder, log, page readers, WhatsApp scripts, download slot
├── Web/
│   ├── TabController        one WKWebView and all its delegates: popups for sign-in, camera and
│   │                        microphone, file uploads, downloads, load errors
│   ├── BridgeScript         injected JS: replaces window.Notification and reports title changes;
│   │                        also holds the Safari user-agent constant
│   ├── IconStore            site icons read from the page, cached in Application Support
│   └── NetworkMonitor       retries failed tabs when the network returns
└── Views/
    ├── MainWindow           hides the window instead of closing it (keeps web views attached)
    ├── WebHost              one container holding every tab's web view; only visible ones shown
    ├── RootView, SidebarView, AddServiceSheet, FindBar, SplitOverlay, QuickSwitcherView
    ├── MenuBarContent, MenuState, AppCommands   menu bar extra and the app menus
    └── SettingsView         General, Notifications, Sleep, Links
Tests/                       XCTest, one file per model type (77 tests)

Services, profiles and tabs

  • A service is a catalog entry: WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook (work), Outlook (personal), OneDrive, Brightspace (asks for the school's address), Reddit, X, GitHub, or a custom website.
  • A profile is one sign-in, backed by one persistent WKWebsiteDataStore. Teams, Outlook (work), OneDrive and Brightspace share the "Microsoft (work)" profile by default; "Add another account" creates a new profile.
  • A tab is a service opened in a profile, with its own name, colour, mute and sleep settings. Incognito tabs use a non-persistent store and are never saved.

Why one container

Every tab's web view stays a subview of one container in the main window, and closing the window only hides it. A web view taken out of its window is throttled by WebKit, which would stop notifications and unread counts from background tabs. For the same reason all tabs load at launch; only tabs that are allowed to sleep (not WhatsApp, Discord, Teams or Outlook by default) are released after the idle time, and a sleeping tab posts no notifications.

Data flow: a new message

  1. The page calls new Notification(…); the injected bridge posts it to the WKScriptMessageHandler.
  2. Unless notifications are paused or the tab is muted, a UNNotificationRequest is posted with the tab's name as subtitle and a per-tab thread. macOS applies Focus.
  3. The page's title changes to "(3) …"; UnreadParser updates the tab's badge, the Dock badge (the total) and the menu bar icon.
  4. Clicking the notification shows the window and selects that tab.

Persistence

  • ~/Library/Application Support/Tabchat/state.json: tabs, profiles, settings, pause end date, split layout, catalog order. Versioned; older files migrate on load.
  • ~/Library/WebKit/com.narendranag.tabchat/: the data stores (cookies, storage) per profile.
  • Login keychain: "Tabchat WebCrypto Master Key", created by WebKit; readable across rebuilds because local builds keep the same signing identity (see 03 Building).

Requirements, development environment, and build commands.

Updated 2026-10-13 · Source 03-building.md · Read first: TabChat for Agents documentation

Building

Requirements

  • macOS 14 Sonoma or later (to run the app; the app targets macOS 14+)
  • Apple Silicon (M1 or later; Intel not supported)
  • Xcode 26 or later (Swift 6; CI uses 26.6, development uses 27)
  • Homebrew (for build tools)

Development environment

Install build tools:

brew install xcodegen swiftlint swiftformat just

These are used by the build recipes:

  • xcodegen: Generates the Xcode project from project.yml
  • swiftlint: Lints Swift code for style and correctness
  • swiftformat: Auto-formats Swift code
  • just: Task runner (like make, but simpler; recipes in justfile)

Build commands

All commands use just to run recipes defined in justfile. The recipes generate the Xcode project (xcodegen) and then run Xcode commands.

Generate Xcode project

just gen

Generates Tabchat.xcodeproj from project.yml. Run this after any change to project.yml or when syncing from remote.

Build

just build

Builds the app for release. Output: build/DerivedData/Build/Products/Release/Tabchat.app.

Run

just run

Builds and runs the app in the simulator or on the current Mac.

Test

just test

Runs XCTest unit and integration tests. Tests are in Tests/.

Lint

just lint

Runs swiftlint to check for style and correctness issues. Errors block CI; warnings are logged.

Format

just format

Auto-formats Swift code with swiftformat. Useful before committing.

Release

just release

Builds the app in Release configuration. Output: build/DerivedData/Build/Products/Release/Tabchat.app.

Packaging

just dmg

Builds the app and packages it as a .dmg installer at build/Tabchat-<version>.dmg, where version is read from the app's CFBundleShortVersionString in Info.plist.

The DMG contains:

  • Tabchat.app: The signed application
  • Applications symlink: For easy installation (drag-and-drop to Applications)

The app is signed with the local Apple Development identity (team 4HL2424MH6). On another Mac without this certificate, Gatekeeper will block the app. To run it:

  • Right-click the app and select "Open"
  • Or go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway

Publishing a release

  1. Bump MARKETING_VERSION (and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION) in project.yml.
  2. just lint && just test && just dmg, then hdiutil verify build/Tabchat-<version>.dmg.
  3. Write brief/release-<version>.md: what's new, requirements, the first-open step, and the dmg's SHA-256 (shasum -a 256).
  4. Tag and publish:
git tag -a v<version> -m "Tabchat for Mac <version>" && git push origin v<version>
gh release create v<version> build/Tabchat-<version>.dmg -R narendranag/tabchat-for-agents \
  --title "Tabchat for Mac <version>" --notes-file brief/release-<version>.md

Releases so far: v0.1.0 (first release), v0.1.1 (GitHub service).

Code signing

Local builds sign with the Apple Development identity of team 4HL2424MH6 (a free Personal Team certificate in the login keychain). A stable identity matters: WebKit keeps a "Tabchat WebCrypto Master Key" in the keychain, and an ad-hoc signature changes on every build, so Keychain would ask for permission after each rebuild.

Without the certificate (CI, another Mac), sign ad-hoc:

TABCHAT_SIGN_IDENTITY=- just build

CI sets TABCHAT_SIGN_IDENTITY=-. Distribution signing (Developer ID, notarisation) is planned.

Development workflow

  1. Clone and install:

    git clone https://github.com/narendranag/tabchat-for-agents.git
cd tabchat
brew install xcodegen swiftlint swiftformat just

  2. Generate and build:

    just gen
just build

  3. Run locally:

    just run

    or open Tabchat.xcodeproj in Xcode and build from there.

  4. Make changes:

    • Edit Swift code in App/Sources/
    • Add or change tests in Tests/
    • If project.yml changes, run just gen again

  5. Before committing:

    just format
just lint
just test

  6. CI/CD:

    • Push to main or open a PR
    • GitHub Actions runs just lint, just test, just build automatically (see .github/workflows/ci.yml)

Debugging

In Xcode

  1. Open Tabchat.xcodeproj
  2. Set breakpoints in Swift code
  3. Run with Cmd+R or the Play button
  4. Use the Debug navigator and console

App logs

The app logs to the standard system log and to ~/Library/Logs/Tabchat/. View with:

log show --predicate 'process == "Tabchat"' --level debug

Planned (not yet built)

  • Developer ID signing and notarisation in CI (needs the paid Apple Developer Program)
  • Sparkle automatic updates, once builds are notarised
  • Intel (x86_64) builds

How local agents read chats and act in TabChat: the socket, the CLI and MCP, the read and act tiers, the WhatsApp scripts, and the security model.

Updated 2026-10-15 · Source 04-agent-api.md · Read first: Overview, Architecture

Agent API

The reasoning (routes considered, terms-of-service risk per service, the decisions) is in brief/agent-api.md in the repo root. This page is how it is built.

Shape

agent (Claude Code, a script…)
  │  tabchat-agent <call> …            or   tabchat-agent mcp  (JSON-RPC over stdio)
  ▼
~/Library/Application Support/Tabchat/agent.sock   (mode 0600, peer uid checked)
  │  one JSON request line → one JSON response line
  ▼
AgentSocketServer → AgentService (main actor)
  ├── AgentResponder     who may read what; tabs, feed           (pure, tested)
  ├── AgentFeed          notifications, in memory, ≤500, ≤24 h
  ├── PageReaders        chat list, page text, debug inspect      (isolated content world)
  ├── WhatsAppScripts    messages, open, download, contact
  └── AgentLog           agent.log: time, program, call, tab, items, outcome — never content

The wire format (Shared/AgentProtocol.swift) and the MCP adapter (Shared/AgentMCP.swift) are compiled into both the app and the tabchat-agent tool, which the app bundle carries in Contents/MacOS/.

Calls

Call Tier Needs Returns
tabs read — readable tabs: id, name, service, unread, loaded
feed read optional tab, sinceSeconds notifications from readable tabs
chats read tab (WhatsApp) chat list; countsOnly gives numbers only
messages read tab (WhatsApp) open chat: id, direction, sender, stamp, time, day, date, text, document, media, rendered
page read tab url, title, visible text (≤20,000 characters)
open act tab, chat opens the chat with that exact name, from the list or through search
contact act tab name, phone, about of the open chat
download act tab, message file: {path, bytes} for the saved document, photo or video
history act tab, optional screens (1–20, default 3) messages read while scrolling back and down again
inspect debug tab, selector element structure (debug builds only)

Text from chats is marked "untrusted": true. There is no call that sends.

Permissions

  • settings.agentAccess — the master switch; off by default. Turning it off stops the socket and forgets the feed.
  • Tab.agentReadable — the read tier, per tab. Incognito tabs are never readable.
  • Tab.agentActions — the actions tier, per tab, only offered for readable tabs.

These keys came without a schema bump, so v0.1.x still opens the state file (it would refuse a newer version and reset the tabs).

WhatsApp scripts

Written against WhatsApp Web's data-testid hooks, learned with inspect on 2026-10-15: #pane-side rows with cell-frame-title; #main messages as [data-id] with msg-container, msg-meta, selectable-text, data-pre-plain-text="[time, date] Sender: ", and document-thumb titled View "<file>"; the document viewer media-viewer-modal with Download and Close buttons; the contact panel chat-info-drawer, opened from conversation-info-header.

  • Direction comes from the status tick in msg-meta (the message-in/out classes are gone).
  • Messages scrolled out of view are drawn as data-virtualized="true"; messages reports them as rendered: false; download scrolls them into view first.
  • open clicks the chat in the list if WhatsApp has drawn it; otherwise it types the name into the search box (chat-list-search-container in #side, a plain text field, never the message box), opens the result with exactly that name, and clears the search. Live-checked 2026-10-15.
  • history scrolls the message list (the nearest scrolling ancestor of the first message) up screens screens, waiting for WhatsApp to load more, then back down, keeping each message the first time it is drawn, placed right after the known message drawn before it (WhatsApp keeps some rows drawn while scrolling). It only scrolls, and ends at the newest message. It is in the actions tier because scrolling back makes WhatsApp fetch older messages. Timers are slowed in a tab that isn't on screen, so it is quicker with the WhatsApp tab selected.
  • download closes any viewer still open, then clicks the document thumb, or for a photo or video the image-thumb, video-content or blob: image, and presses Download in the viewer. It checks that the saved file has the document's name (allowing the 1 added for a duplicate) and answers ok: false with the path when it doesn't. Photos are live-checked (image-thumb, 2026-10-15); an album downloads its first photo; videos are not checked yet.
  • WhatsApp stamps text messages with their day but not documents or photos. day is the divider above the message in the list ("Today", "Friday", "27/09/2026"; English only). date comes from the stamp, else from day (weekday names count back from today), else from the dated messages on either side when both are on the same day; otherwise it is absent.
  • The CLI waits up to 120 seconds for actions (15 for reads).
  • Downloads go through the tab's WKDownload handling, redirected by an AgentDownloadSlot to ~/Downloads/Tabchat/<service>/<contact>/, and are quarantined.

Each script is tested in XCTest against an invented page (Tests/AgentTests.swift, Tests/AgentActionTests.swift). When WhatsApp changes its page, a script returns {"ok": false, "reason": …} rather than a guess; fix the selectors with inspect in a debug build.

Live checks

Run against the debug build, with the services ticked in Settings → Agents:

TA=build/DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug/Tabchat.app/Contents/MacOS/tabchat-agent
$TA tabs
$TA chats --tab <id> --counts-only
$TA inspect --tab <id> --selector '#main'

Never paste real chat content, names or numbers into the repo, tests or issues.
